 © 2026 Yahoo. All rights reserved. The Washington Wizards are set to return to the floor tonight, yet they got good news on the status of two players ahead of tipoff.
 Both center Alex Sarr and guard Bub Carrington are available to play on Sunday, per the updated NBA injury report. Washington will be without one after head coach Brian Keefe revealed in his pregame availability that guard Tre Johnson will be inactive due to lower back soreness. The status of rookie forward Felix Okpara remains unclear ahead of tipoff. Okpara owns a two-way designation with the Capital City Go-Go, the Wizards' G League affiliate, fresh off their home opener on Saturday while they return to action on Monday afternoon.
 Advertisement Advertisement Advertisement Yet the status of Sarr and Carrington serves as a notable boost to the rotation given Sarr has started in all 12 games he has been available. Sarr, who was ruled questionable due to illness, is averaging 11.2 points and 7.4 rebounds across over 27 minutes per game. Carrington was ruled questionable due to a chest contusion, but now enters tipoff with a chance to keep his active streak alive. Carrington owns the NBA's third longest active streak with Sunday set to be the Baltimore native's 178th consecutive game played. The third year guard is transitioning into his role in the Wizards' second unit, but is also one of three players in NBA history to notch at least 700 assists on 300 made three pointers prior to his 21st birthday. Carrington is averaging nearly five points across 18 minutes per game.
 Reece Beekman, Justin Champagnie, Tristan Vukcevic and Jamir Watkins all remain sidelined, as expected.
 The Rockets will enter tipoff with a notable boost to the lineup with veteran center Steven Adams also upgraded and ruled available ahead of tipoff. Adams drew a questionable designation after suffering a right soleus strain with Sunday marking his first appearance since logging eight minutes against the San Antonio Spurs back on October 23, his lone game during the 2026-27 regular season. The Rockets remain without Clint Capela, Quadir Copeland, Julian Phillips and Fred VanVleet while Marcus Smart is set to serve his league suspension, also sidelining him tonight.
 While Washington owns a 4-9 record and looks to end a six game losing streak in addition to climbing back to .500 inside Capital One Arena, head coach Brian Keefe is tasked with slowing down a Rockets team fresh off three consecutive wins and owning a 10-3 record ahead of tipoff.
